title: REGENERATION × ECA attractor recovery (n=4 ring) — k-bit perturbation T_recovery sweep
question: Across a panel of n=4 ECA substrates, does a k-bit perturbation of an attractor state recover (re-enter the attractor set) with a T_recovery that scales non-trivially (≥1.5×) with k?
engine: pure hexa-lang (no IIT4 import); deterministic forward step on a 4-cell periodic ECA ring; attractor set built by 70-step burn-in then collecting 30 subsequent states
runtime: $0 pool ubu-2 · hexa-only · LLM none · NO GPU · deterministic (cross-process byte-identical)

rule_110.note: single fixed-point attractor at 0; every k-bit flip drops into a different basin and never returns within 50 steps

rule_30.note: single fixed point 5; perturbations also fixed points of different basins

rule_60.note: ONLY substrate with finite recovery; XOR-class rule pulls perturbations back into the all-zeros basin

rule_204_anchor.note: identity rule (sanity); every state is its own fixed point so perturbed states are fixed-but-different — T=-1 confirms the measurement honestly reports 'different basin' rather than spuriously matching

falsifier_eval.F327_1_RECOVERY_FINITE: PARTIAL — only rule_60 returns finite T_recovery for any k; rule_110/30/204 all -1
falsifier_eval.F327_2_K_SCALING_GE_1_5x: FAIL — rule_60 T values {4,3,4}; max/min ratio = 4/3 ≈ 1.33 < 1.5 threshold (and non-monotone)
falsifier_eval.F327_4_ANCHOR_SANITY: PASS — rule_204 identity gives T=-1 as required (would have been a tautology bug if it returned 0)

verdict_derived: 🔴 FALSIFIED — H1 (T_recovery scales ≥1.5× with k) is decisively falsified. n=4 ECA panel is dominated by single-point attractors; only rule_60 admits any recovery and even there the k-scaling is 1.33× non-monotone. The decisive sanity (rule_204 anchor returning T=-1) proves the measurement could have falsified or supported either way — it is not a tautology smoke.
structural_vs_dynamical: DYNAMICAL kernel (forward timestep loop + attractor detection) yet result 🔴 — the first DYNAMICAL cell to falsify, refines H_326 raster claim that DYNAMICAL kernels enjoy a higher SUPP-rate: not unconditional, depends on the scale being large enough to admit a non-trivial recovery regime. At n=4 the recovery axis collapses.
honest_limits: n=4 panel is too small to admit non-trivial multi-state attractor cycles; n≥6 with rule 110/30 would likely show genuine cycle attractors and richer T_recovery(k) curves
Single starting seed s0=5; a sweep over s0 ∈ {1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15} (odd-parity states) would harden the falsification
step_cap=50 — a 'never recovers within 50 steps' verdict for rule_110 may flip with larger caps; but the H1 threshold (1.5× scaling) is decoupled from the cap and remains falsified regardless
